lines.trans: They say it is raining where Cindy is right now, yet she is pitching a tent and sleeping outdoors.

words.gloss: they say it is coming down

lines.trans: Because she lost rock-paper-scissors, they say Cindy carried all the bags up herself.
What is wrong? Looks like the footage will be fun, though?
It just reminds me of the old days—think back to when the veteran actresses were here.
Could something like this ever possibly happen?
Imagine telling them to sleep outdoors in the rain—they would ask if we had all lost our minds!
It only turned out like that because Baek Seung-chan is clumsy and clueless about how things work.
If he were a savvy kid, how would he ever dare treat Cindy like that?
In the middle of all this, he is not going to make her play the dinner game of chance too, right?
Oh come on, surely not—give him a call right now!

examples.trans: What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Used with 오다 or 내리다.

examples.trans: It is raining.
The rain stopped.

meanings.en: to come (of a feeling, state, or weather)
meanings.note: Used in expressions like 혼란이 오다 (confusion comes) or 비가 오다 (rain falls)

examples.text: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
examples.trans: It's been one year since I came to Korea.
I suddenly started feeling sleepy.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그런데; introduces a contrast or obstacle.
Used to shift the topic in conversation.

examples.trans: By the way, what time is it now?
I want to go. But I don't have time.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Do you not need a shot of her pitching the tent?
Here the word for 'tent' is key.

meanings.en: to hit, to strike, to cause (trouble)
meanings.note: Used in idioms like 사고를 치다 (to cause trouble).

examples.trans: I caused trouble.
I caused trouble. (2)
The weather was nice, so we ate outdoors.
There is a lot of outdoor filming.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 지금 신디네 비 온대요, 근데 텐트 치고 야외 취침한대요.
examples.trans: They say it is raining where Cindy is right now, yet she is pitching a tent and sleeping outdoors.
This expression comes from 'they say she is sleeping'.

examples.text: 우리 가위바위보 해서 서로 짐 들어 주기 할까요?
examples.trans: Shall we play rock-paper-scissors to carry each other's bags?

examples.text: 저 가위 낼게요. 안 내면 진 거, 가위바위보!
examples.trans: I am going to throw scissors. Lose if you don't throw—rock, paper, scissors!

examples.text: 저 가위 낼게요. 안 내면 진 거, 가위바위보!
examples.trans: I am going to throw scissors. Lose if you don't throw—rock, paper, scissors!

examples.text: 가위바위보 해서 져서 내가 하루 종일 들고 다니는 걸로 찍혔잖아요.
examples.trans: I lost rock-paper-scissors and was already filmed carrying them all day.

examples.text: 어제는 술 먹고 들이닥친 거고 오늘은 짐 들어 준 거잖아.
examples.trans: Yesterday he barged in drunk, and today he just carried my bags.

examples.text: 우리 가위바위보 해서 서로 짐 들어 주기 할까요?
examples.trans: Shall we play rock-paper-scissors to carry each other's bags?

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.
If it's heavy, I'll carry it.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 가위바위보에서 졌다고 신디가 짐도 다 들고 올라갔대요.
examples.trans: Because she lost rock-paper-scissors, they say Cindy carried all the bags up herself.
This expression comes from 'they say she went up'.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Do you not need a shot of her pitching the tent?
Here the word for 'footage, visual shot' is key.

meanings.en: to be fun, to be entertaining
meanings.note: Spoken contraction of 재미있다.

examples.trans: This movie is really fun.
Studying Korean is fun.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 예전 생각이 나서 그래, 예전에 선생님들 계실 때 생각해 봐.
examples.trans: It just reminds me of the old days—think back to when the veteran actresses were here.
Here the word for 'old days, past' is key.

meanings.note: noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.

meanings.en: to arise, to come up, to occur
meanings.note: Used with feelings, thoughts, or events (e.g. 실감이 나다, 생각이 나다).

examples.trans: A good idea came to mind.
Tears suddenly came to my eyes.

meanings.note: respectful term for teacher or senior

examples.trans: Hello teacher.
Good teacher.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.
Let's I think together today.
I worked hard to I think yesterday too.

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.

meanings.note: Demonstrative pronoun for something near the speaker; often contracted to 이거 in speech.

examples.trans: Did you film this too?
How much is this?

있다.gloss: to exist, to have, to stay

meanings.en: to exist, to be (in a place)
meanings.note: Opposite of 없다.
Marks the possessed item with 이/가.

examples.trans: Do you have time?
Nobody is at home.

related.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.note: Bound noun used in -(으)ㄹ 수 있다/없다 ('can / cannot').

examples.trans: I can read Korean.
I cannot go today.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean numeral used with counters and in numbers

examples.trans: Let's meet in the first-floor lobby.

examples.text: 일 호선이 가장 오래된 지하철 노선이에요.
examples.trans: Line 1 is the oldest subway line.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Colloquial spoken form of 너희네; used among close friends or to juniors.

examples.text: 너네 오늘 수업 몇 시에 끝나?
examples.trans: What time does your class end today?
You guys all come over here together.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 비 오는데 야외 취침하라고 했어 봐, 너네 다 돌았냐고!
examples.trans: Imagine telling them to sleep outdoors in the rain—they would ask if we had all lost our minds!
This expression comes from 'have you gone crazy!'.

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 백승찬이 애가 어리바리하고 물정을 모르니까 일이 그렇게 됐지.
examples.trans: It only turned out like that because Baek Seung-chan is clumsy and clueless about how things work.
This expression comes from 'is bumbling and'.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 백승찬이 애가 어리바리하고 물정을 모르니까 일이 그렇게 됐지.
examples.trans: It only turned out like that because Baek Seung-chan is clumsy and clueless about how things work.
Here the word for 'how the world works' is key.

meanings.en: to not know, to be unaware of
meanings.note: 르-irregular verb: stem 모르- + -아요/-았어요 → 몰라요 / 몰랐어요.

examples.trans: I don't know well either.
I didn't realize time was passing.
Please don't say it like that.
It's not that difficult compared to what I thought.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 요령 있는 애였어 봐, 감히 신디한테 어떻게 그러니?
examples.trans: If he were a savvy kid, how would he ever dare treat Cindy like that?
Here the word for 'knack, street smarts' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 요령 있는 애였어 봐, 감히 신디한테 어떻게 그러니?
examples.trans: If he were a savvy kid, how would he ever dare treat Cindy like that?
Here the word for 'daringly' is key.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 이 와중에 저녁 복불복까지 하겠다 그러는 거 아니겠죠?
examples.trans: In the middle of all this, he is not going to make her play the dinner game of chance too, right?
Here the word for 'in the middle of' is key.

meanings.note: The time of day from late afternoon into night.
Short for 저녁 식사 or 저녁밥.

examples.trans: Did you eat dinner?
Let's meet this evening.

examples.text: 가면 저녁밥 복불복 게임 하실 겁니다.
examples.trans: Once we arrive, you will play a game of chance for dinner.
The topic of game of luck came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Negative copula used with nouns (often with -이/가)

examples.trans: It is not my fault.
Today is not Sunday, it's Monday.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (interj).

examples.text: 아유 설마, 전화 좀 해 봐!
examples.trans: Oh come on, surely not—give him a call right now!
Here the word for 'oh goodness' is key.

examples.text: 선? 검사? 설마 검사가 예쁘기까지 하겠어?
examples.trans: A blind date? A prosecutor? Could a prosecutor really be pretty too?

examples.text: 설마 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (surely not, could it be), we will get good results.

meanings.note: Sino-Korean word for telephone.

examples.trans: A phone call came.
I will hang up the phone.
Please give me some water.
Please wait just a moment.

meanings.note: Contraction of 조금
Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.

meanings.note: Used when repeating an action.

examples.trans: See you again!
It is raining again.

meanings.note: Action of coming together with someone.

examples.trans: I meet a friend.
Let's meet tomorrow.
